VICE TIMELINE Cover Studio

Turn any photo into a magazine-style Vice cover — now the bottom-heavy studio: a new Bottom Heavy layout puts two 50/50 panels across the top 20%, a dark title band across the middle 15% with the big centred title, and a full-width hero photo across the bottom 65% (tagline + credits ride over the hero's foot on a dark scrim); Auto-caption v3 adds three new styles — Retro Ad (1980s ad copy), Breaking News (the emergency headline) and Album Liner (the record sleeve) — so the panel now offers nine caption cards; and Tilt Pro adds three new presets — Poster Lean, Billboard and Phone Tilt — plus a shadow-style picker (soft, hard, neon glow) that bakes into every export with tilt on. The twenty-third template, Vice Bottom Heavy, shows the whole v21 axis in one click: Bottom Heavy, a Breaking News caption, the Billboard tilt and a neon-glow shadow inside a cyan Neon Border. Underneath it all, the centre-stage studio: a new Center Stage layout puts the big photo dead centre (50% wide) between two 25% side panels, under a full-width title band across the top 38% of the cover with the title centred in it like a headliner above the stage, and two new frames — Gold Foil (a metallic gold border with a diagonal gradient and a shine band) and Blueprint (a blueprint-blue border with a fine grid, corner crosshairs and a SCALE 1:1 • VICE STUDIO label) — bring the frame count to eleven. Three new procedural stickers — a palm tree, a smiling sun and a cassette tape — bring the sticker count to thirteen, each with its own colour and a 0.5×–2× size slider. The twenty-second template, Vice Center Stage, shows the whole v20 axis in one click: Center Stage, the Golden Coast Look, gold Title FX, and the Gold Foil frame with a palm-tree sticker. Underneath it all, the timeline studio: every undo step shows as a labelled thumbnail in the History Timeline (click any step to jump straight back to it — Undo is no longer blind), a Hero Left layout puts the big hero photo on the left 60% with two stacked panels on the right and the title in a dark band under the hero, and two frames — Comic Burst (thick black comic border with POW! / BAM! burst stars and halftone dots) and Retro TV (a grey CRT bezel with an antenna, channel knobs, a speaker grille and a CH 06 strip). The twenty-first template, Vice Timeline, shows the v19 axis in one click: Hero Left, the Golden Coast Look, a Tagline Punch caption, and the Comic Burst frame. Underneath it all, the layouts studio: two new layouts bring the count to 20 — Quad Grid (four vertical strips at uneven 25/35/25/15 widths, the second strip reading as the hero column) and Split Screen (two 50/50 halves split by a glowing neon divider that the big centred title straddles, tagline and credits centred on it too); Auto-caption v2 adds three new deterministic styles — Tagline Punch (a short loud slogan), Movie Credit Line (a film-poster billing block under the title) and Neon Slogan (a neon slogan keyed off the title word) — so the panel now offers nine caption cards (v3 adds Retro Ad, Breaking News and Album Liner), and each v2/v3 card applies title + tagline + cover lines in one click; and two new Looks bring the count to 8 — Vice Noir (high-contrast monochrome + heavy grain, flat white-on-black title) and Golden Coast (warm pastel beach light + soft vignette, gradient title). The twentieth template, Vice Layouts, shows the whole v18 axis in one click: Split Screen, the Vice Noir Look, a Neon Slogan tagline, and a cyan Neon Border. Two fixes ride along in v18: the Split Screen title block is centred on the divider (before, every layout's title sat left-aligned, so the divider had nothing to straddle), and panel caption text now starts past the Neon Border's edge instead of hiding its first letter under the frame. Underneath it all, the studio-pro studio: export at ANY size you type (up to 4096 per side, aspect-lock toggle, plus one-click presets for an X header 1500×500, a LinkedIn banner 1584×396 and an ultrawide 2560×1080 wallpaper — the cover re-renders at that size, never a crop); colour-theory harmony suggestions read your photo's dominant colour and offer Complementary, Analogous and Triadic schemes that recolour the whole title (marker + outline + shadow) in one click; and two new frames — a Neon Border with a glow colour you pick, and a VHS Frame with PLAY ▶, an SP 0:00:00 timecode, a tracking bar and a VICE CITY • VHS foot strip, both baked into every PNG. The nineteenth template, Vice Studio Pro, shows the whole v17 axis in one click: Banner Cinema, a Triadic harmony from Vice orange, and a cyan Neon Border. Underneath it all, the bundle studio: one “Download ZIP” click packs all 11 outputs into a single ZIP file (hand-written offline ZIP writer, STORE + real CRC32 — no library, no network), so the whole set leaves in one download instead of eleven; two new layouts — Triptych Wide (wide panorama over two panels) and Vertical Strip (three stacked panels beside a sideways title band) — bring the layout count to 17; five new procedural stickers (crown, sunglasses, flame, dice, sparkle star — 10 kinds total) each with its own colour picker; and the eighteenth template, Vice Bundle, shows the whole v16 axis in one click: Triptych Wide, Bebas Neue chrome title over a yellow marker with a hot-pink outline and a cyan shadow, and three new-kind stickers. Two fixes ride along in v17: the VHS Frame is now a mat (like Film Strip) so its bars never cover the masthead, title or panel captions, and the Banner Cinema title shrinks when a wide cover would otherwise push its credits off the bottom edge. Underneath it all, the polish studio: Title FX puts a marker highlight, a coloured outline and a drop shadow behind the big title lettering (all baked into the PNG); two new film presets — Kodachrome (warm + punchy) and Fuji 400H (soft pastel) — join the Photo Lab; keyboard shortcuts (Ctrl/⌘+Z undo, Ctrl/⌘+S export-all, arrow keys nudge the selected freeform item, Delete removes the selected sticker or bubble) speed up every edit; and the A/B compare panel wipes between the cover you are editing now and the last cover you exported, on a draggable divider. The seventeenth template, Vice Polish, shows the v15 axis in one click. The eighteenth template, Vice Bundle, shows the v16 axis in one click: Triptych Wide, Bebas chrome, Title FX highlight + outline + shadow, and three new stickers (crown, shades, sparkle). Magazine layout, Anton title over a yellow marker with a hot-pink outline and a cyan shadow, Kodachrome film. Underneath it all, the complete studio: one “Export everything” click saves all 11 outputs at once — 4 post sizes, the contact sheet, all 3 mockups and all 3 print sizes — with a live progress bar; three real OFL display fonts (Anton, Archivo Black, and Bebas Neue, the tall movie-poster face) with one-click font pairings; and two new layouts, Grid 2×2 and the cinematic Banner with its dark title band. Underneath it all, real print sizes — A4 portrait 2480×3508 (300 dpi), A3 landscape 4961×3508 (300 dpi) and a 24×36″ poster 2400×3600 (100 dpi), all PNG — stamp your own logo on it as a watermark (your own PNG, 5 positions, size + opacity, baked into every export), and keep every cover you make in the session gallery (thumbnail + name + time, click to load it back into the editor). The fifteenth template, Vice Print, shows the print axis in one click: Showcase layout, chrome Anton title, print marks on. The sixteenth template, Vice Complete, shows the v14 axis in one click: Banner layout, chrome Bebas Neue title, Tall & Tight pairing. Underneath it all, real 3D tilt: lean the whole finished cover in perspective (tilt X/Y ±20°, camera distance, eight one-click presets and three shadow styles — soft, hard, neon glow — the depth is baked into the PNG, not a CSS trick) and present it as a Framed Poster, a Phone Screen, or a night Billboard — three procedural mockup exports, drawn in code with no assets. The new Showcase layout is built for the tilt: one framed photo on a sunset stage with the big title in the band below it. The fourteenth template, Vice Showcase, shows the whole new axis in one click. Underneath it all, three real OFL display fonts (Anton + Archivo Black + Bebas Neue, vendored locally, no network) for the big poster lettering: pick the title face and the tagline face — or a ready font pairing in one click — pair any of them with all 7 title styles including Chrome Gradient, and try the new Banner layout — a wide panorama over a dark title band — or the Sunset Strip layout — one wide photo strip over a giant title on a sunset gradient band. The thirteenth template, Vice Fonts, shows that axis in one click. Underneath it all, the freeform editor: pick any layout, switch Freeform on, and drag every photo anywhere on the canvas — resize it from a corner handle, rotate it from the ring above it, bring it forward or send it back, with pink snap guides when it lines up with the canvas centre or edge — and drag the title block itself to any spot, tilted as you like; every move, resize and rotation bakes into the PNG. Behind the panels the canvas background can be a solid colour, a 2-stop gradient (from your custom palette in one click), or a faint dots or grid pattern, and Print marks add a bleed edge, crop marks and a safe-area box to the export, so the cover is print-ready. The twelfth template, Vice Freeform, shows that axis in one click. Underneath it all, Batch mode still builds 6 different covers from 6 photos at once — each photo is read from its own pixels (brightness, contrast, warmth, dominant colour), and its grade, layout, title and frame are picked for that photo, so no two covers in the batch look alike — then export all six as 1080×1080 PNGs in one click. Eleven procedural frames border any cover and bake into the PNG — Film Strip with sprocket holes, Polaroid with a caption foot, Ticket Stub with perforations and ADMIT ONE, Torn Edge with a jagged paper border, Rounded with cut corners, Neon Border with a glow in your colour, VHS Frame with PLAY + SP timecode and a tracking bar, Comic Burst with burst stars and halftone dots, Retro TV with a CRT bezel, antenna and channel knobs, Gold Foil with a metallic gold gradient and shine band, and Blueprint with a fine grid, crosshairs and a SCALE 1:1 label — and Smart Crop finds each photo's focus point (brightest, busiest region) and steers the panel crop onto it. The eleventh template, Vice Batch, shows the batch axis in one click. Underneath it all, the Palette Builder extracts the 5 dominant colours from your photo's real pixels, you pick 3 stops, and the grade becomes a custom gradient in those colours — save up to 4 palettes of your own, or start from 3 presets (Vice Sunset, Neon Nights, Palm Noir). Pin photos to the Moodboard scrapbook with tape corners, gold pins and handwritten captions, remix the cover every day with Cover of the Day (one deterministic recipe per date), and export all four sizes on one contact sheet. The tenth template, Vice Palette, shows the whole new axis in one click. Underneath it all, the CRT/VHS glitch (chromatic RGB split, scanlines, tracking noise, glitch slices and an RGB fringe on the title — every effect with its own switch and strength, rendered into the pixels and baked into the PNG, with VHS Tracking, CRT Split and Full Glitch presets in one click), Auto-caption (reads your photo's real pixels and writes nine ready titles with matching taglines — deterministic, so the same photo always suggests the same nine — and one click applies title + tagline, or title + tagline + cover lines for the v2 and v3 styles), and procedural stickers (star, lightning bolt, mini palm, sun, neon heart, palm tree, smiling sun, cassette) peel-and-stick onto the cover with a die-cut white edge, draggable anywhere, up to 6 at once. Export adds a fourth size — 1080×1920 vertical story — alongside 1080×1080, 1080×1350 and 1920×1080, and export-all saves all four PNGs at once, or one contact sheet with all four on it. The Darkroom gives you a draggable tone curve (Luma, Red, Green, Blue — click to add a point, drag to move it, double-click to remove it), exposure, contrast, saturation, temperature, highlights, shadows, sharpen and clarity sliders, plus per-colour HSL shifts — all live in the preview and baked into the PNG. Smart Suggest reads your photo's real pixels and recommends the grade, layout and title that fit it best, as three one-click cards. The Diptych layout makes the cover itself a before/after — raw photo on the left, developed cover on the right, labelled BEFORE / AFTER. The Cross Process treatment develops the film in the wrong chemicals (blue shadows, warm highlights), and Golden Hour / Blue Hour presets apply a full darkroom recipe in one click. The Procedural Art Kit paints sunburst rays, palm and skyline silhouettes, a sun disc and a perspective grid floor straight onto the cover in code (no assets, no uploads), speech/thought bubbles add comic dialogue you can drag anywhere, and the Storyboard layout tells the story in 4 numbered panels. Projects save and reload as one JSON file (photos included) and autosave in the browser, so a cover is never lost. Series mode builds a main cover plus a square and a portrait variant from one theme — change the theme once and all three follow, then export the whole series as 3 PNGs in one click. The Photo Lab adds background blur, a spotlight, color-pop (one hue stays vivid, the rest drains away) and five vintage film presets (VHS 86, Polaroid 95, Chrome 99, Kodachrome, Fuji 400H); the template gallery shows twenty-three finished covers as painted thumbnails, so you see the recipe before you click it; and a 3-step guided wizard (Foto → Gaya → Export) walks new users through, with the full editor always one click away. The v5 grade Sunset Noir (dark + orange rim) joins 11 other grades, and the title engine keeps 7 styles including Chrome Gradient. Eight one-click Looks apply a complete cover recipe (layout + grade + backdrop + title style + treatment); the Magazine layout is a full-bleed single photo under the masthead. Underneath it all, the v2 Ink engine still turns any panel into comic-book art (posterize + edge ink + halftone dots, level adjustable per panel), with 22 layouts, 12 sunset/neon grades, 3 built-in Vice City scene backdrops with blend modes, per-panel captions, duotone/threshold/solarize/cross-process treatments, light-leak + vignette, a before/after compare slider, Surprise me + 20-step undo with a visible History Timeline, and one-click PNG export in 1080×1080, 1080×1350, 1920×1080 and 1080×1920 — or all four sizes at once, or one contact sheet. Built by an AI agent for make.fun's “Make GTA 6 Cover Art” bounty, $250 in USDC.

Step 1 — load a photo (or use a sample), then press Next. Jump to the full editor any time: every control below stays live.

1 · Photos (up to 3)
1b · Batch mode — 6 photos, 6 different covers

Upload up to 6 photos at once and the studio builds a different cover for each — grade, layout, title and frame are picked from that photo's own pixels, so no two covers in the batch look alike. Export batch saves all six as 1080×1080 PNGs. Without uploads, Build batch uses your editor photos + scene backdrops.

2 · Looks — one click

A full cover recipe per preset: layout + grade + backdrop + title style + treatment.

2d · History Timeline — every undo step, visible

Undo is no longer blind: every change you make appears here as a small thumbnail of the cover as it was before that change, labelled with what changed. Click any thumbnail to jump straight back to that step — the steps after it are dropped, like scrubbing a timeline. The last tile is the cover as it is now.

No steps yet — change something (a Look, a layout, a frame) and each step appears here as a thumbnail you can jump back to.

2b · Template gallery — see it, then click it

Twenty-two finished covers as thumbnails — layout + grade + title + Photo Lab in one click. Unlike Looks, you see the result before you pick it.

2c · Series mode — 3 covers, one theme

One theme, three covers at once: the main cover (landscape) plus a square and a portrait variant, each with its own layout. Change the theme once and all three follow; “Export series” saves all three PNGs.

3 · Title engine

Happy with the type? The same Export everything as section 9 — all 4 post sizes, the contact sheet, all 3 mockups and all 3 print sizes, one click.

3a · Title FX — marker highlight, outline & shadow

The marker swipe sits behind each title word; the outline re-colours the letter edge; the shadow drops a flat offset copy behind the word. Pick a colour and its switch turns itself on — everything here bakes into the PNG.

3b · Shortcuts — keyboard

Work faster without the mouse:

  • Ctrl/⌘ Z — Undo the last change
  • Ctrl/⌘ S — Export all 4 sizes (PNG)
  • ← → ↑ ↓ — Nudge the selected freeform item 1px (Shift + arrow: 10px)
  • Delete — Remove the selected sticker or bubble

Click a sticker or bubble — in its list or on the preview — to select it first. Arrow keys only move things while Freeform mode is on.

3c · A/B compare — now vs last exported cover

Compare the cover in the editor now against the last cover you exported (from the session gallery). Drag the divider to wipe between them — left is the last export, right is now.

No exported cover yet — export a cover (or save one to the gallery) and the last one appears here for comparison.

◂ ▸
LAST EXPORT
NOW
4 · Layout
4b · Freeform — move anything, print-ready

Switch Freeform on and the layout grid lets go: drag any panel on the preview to move it, drag a corner handle to resize it, drag the cyan ring above it to rotate it — pink snap guides appear when its centre or edge lines up with the canvas. The title block drags too, anywhere, at any angle. Z-order, print marks and the canvas background all live here, and every change bakes into the PNG.

4c · 3D Tilt & Mockups — depth + presentation

Tilt the whole finished cover in real perspective — it leans, the far edge shrinks, and a shadow lifts it off the board. Eight one-click presets (Flat, Lean left/right, Pop-out, Showcase lean, Poster Lean, Billboard, Phone Tilt) and three shadow styles (soft layered blur, hard solid slab, neon glow) — the tilt and its shadow bake into every PNG export. The Showcase layout is built for it: one framed photo on a sunset stage. Mockups drop the finished cover into a framed poster, a phone screen, or a night billboard — all drawn in code, no assets.

Shadow style — how the floating cover casts its shadow (bakes into every export with tilt on):
4d · Logo / watermark — your mark on the cover

Upload your own logo (PNG — transparency works) and it stamps onto the finished cover: pick a corner or the bottom centre, set the size and opacity, and it bakes into every PNG export, print size, mockup and contact sheet. No logo is used until you upload one — nothing is uploaded anywhere, the file never leaves your machine.

No logo

5 · Grade
5b · Frames — border treatments, baked into the PNG

Eleven procedural frames for the whole cover — Film Strip with sprocket holes, Polaroid with a caption foot, Ticket Stub with perforations and ADMIT ONE, Torn Edge with a jagged paper border, Rounded with cut corners, Neon Border with a glowing edge in your colour, VHS Frame with PLAY + SP timecode and a tracking bar, Comic Burst with burst stars and halftone dots, Retro TV with a CRT bezel, antenna and channel knobs, Gold Foil with a metallic gold gradient and shine band, and Blueprint with a fine grid, crosshairs and a SCALE 1:1 label. The frame is drawn over the finished cover, so it reads on every export size.

Only used by the Neon Border frame — pick the glow colour.

5b · Palette — your colours, your grade

Extract the 5 dominant colours from your photo, then pick 3 stops — the grade tint becomes a gradient in your colours, baked into the PNG. Click a swatch to set the active stop (click a stop picker first to choose which one). Save up to 4 palettes of your own.

Presets — one click, editable after:

5c · Color harmony — theory from your photo

Colour theory from your photo's dominant colour — three schemes, computed in code, no guessing: Complementary (opposites on the wheel, maximum pop), Analogous (neighbours, one calm family) and Triadic (a third of the wheel apart, the loud Vice look). One click applies a scheme to the whole title at once — marker highlight + outline + drop shadow — so the title always matches the photo.

No harmonies yet — press “Suggest harmonies from photo” (needs a photo loaded).

6 · Treatment

A print treatment over the graded photo — duotone, threshold or solarize.

6b · Photo Lab

Darkroom tools over the graded photo — blur softens the photo behind the title, spotlight lights the middle of each panel, color-pop keeps one hue vivid, and the film presets age the print.

6d · Darkroom — tone curve + light

A real darkroom: drag the tone curve, tune the light, shift each colour's hue. Everything renders live and exports into the PNG — the Diptych layout shows the raw photo next to the developed one.

Click the curve to add a point, drag a point to move it, double-click a point to remove it. Luma moves all channels; Red, Green and Blue move one channel.

6e · Smart Suggest — the app reads your photo

Smart Suggest samples the photo's real pixels — brightness, contrast, warmth and dominant colour — and recommends the grade, layout and title that fit it best. One click applies a suggestion.

6f · Glitch / CRT — VHS effects, baked into the PNG

CRT and VHS glitch, rendered into the pixels — chromatic RGB split, scanlines, tracking noise, displaced slices and an RGB fringe on the title. Every effect has its own switch and strength, and all of them export into the PNG. Presets set a whole recipe at once.

6g · Auto-caption — titles from your photo

The same pixel reading as Smart Suggest, turned into titles: warm night, bright gold, cool blue — nine ready captions, one click applies title + tagline. The three v2 styles (Tagline Punch, Movie Credit Line, Neon Slogan) and the three v3 styles (Retro Ad, Breaking News, Album Liner) also set the cover lines, so the whole cover voice changes together. Deterministic: the same photo always suggests the same nine.

6c · Procedural Art Kit — drawn art, no assets

Art drawn in code over the panels — sunburst rays, palm and skyline silhouettes, a sun disc, a perspective grid floor. Each element has its own opacity, colour and scale; drag the position sliders to move it. The art exports into the PNG.

7 · Scene backdrop

A Vice City scene behind the panels — pick a blend to wash its colour over the photos.

8 · Crop, caption & ink per panel

Click a panel number, drag the photo in the preview to move it, zoom with the slider. Every panel gets its own story line — and its own comic-ink treatment.

Panel 1 of 4

Smart crop reads the selected panel's photo, finds its focus point (brightest, busiest region), and steers the crop onto it — the same photo always focuses the same place.

8b · Speech bubbles — comic dialogue

Bubbles sit on top of the cover. Edit the text, pick speech or thought, pick a style — then drag the bubble on the preview to move it anywhere.

8c · Stickers — peel-and-stick art

Thirteen procedural stickers — star, lightning bolt, mini palm, sun, neon heart, crown, sunglasses, flame, dice, sparkle star, palm tree, smiling sun, cassette — drawn in code with a die-cut white edge, so they read on any photo. Pick each sticker's colour, size (0.5×–2× slider) and rotation, drag any sticker on the preview to place it; up to 6 at once.

9 · Export PNG

Custom size — any width × height up to 4096 per side. The cover re-renders at exactly that size (same layout, title, FX and frame — never a crop). Presets jump to a social size in one click.

9b · Print sizes — A4 / A3 / Poster (PNG)

The same finished cover at real print sizes — A4 portrait 2480×3508 (300 dpi), A3 landscape 4961×3508 (300 dpi) and a 24×36″ poster 2400×3600 (100 dpi). Still PNG, as the brief asks. A3 is 17.4 megapixels, so each size takes a few seconds to render — they export one at a time. Tip: switch Print marks on (section 4b) and the bleed edge, crop marks and safe area print with the cover.

10b · Session gallery — this session's covers

Every cover you export lands here automatically, with a thumbnail, a name and a time — click any cover to load that exact version back into the editor. Saved in this session only (in memory, not on disk), so it never follows you into the next visit.

Nothing saved yet — export a cover, or press “Save current cover to gallery”.

10 · Project — save & load

Save the whole cover — layout, grade, art kit, bubbles, captions and photos — as one JSON file, and load it back any time. Your work also autosaves in this browser and comes back when you reopen the page.

Autosave: on — restores your last cover when you reopen.

Live preview — drag the photo to reposition it inside the selected panel, or switch Freeform on and drag any panel or the title anywhere.
